mainTopic: Stories of prayer for rain: why רבה's generation is not answered as רב יהודה's was, and how רבא, רב פפא and רבי חנינא בן דוסא brought rain.
overview: This amud is about how prayers for rain are answered and how much depends on the person praying and on the generation. רבה finishes his speech: his generation learns far more than רב יהודה's did, yet רב יהודה brought rain just by removing one shoe, while רבה's generation cries all day with no answer. רבה concludes that the leaders are not at fault; the generation as a whole is not worthy. The גמרא then tells the story behind the shoe, and רב מרי adds that at the same time angels turned sand into flour, which he told people not to buy. Next come more rain stories: רבא in הגרוניא is helped by a dream, רבא brings rain in תמוז to answer King שבור's test and is then warned by his father, and רב פפא's embarrassment brings rain when his fast had not. רבי חנינא בן דוסא stops and restarts the rain with a few words, and רב יוסף says his prayer was stronger than the כהן גדול's, whose prayer asked that travelers not be listened to. The amud ends by praising רבי חנינא, whose merit feeds the world while he lives on carobs, and begins a story about his wife and their empty oven, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier generation learned only one order; we learn all six
steps.stepSummary: רבה contrasts רב יהודה's generation, whose learning was mostly in נזיקין, with his own generation, which learns all six סדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their learning was in נזיקין, and we learn all six orders of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is finishing a sentence from the previous page. רב יהודה's generation studied mainly סדר נזיקין, while רבה's generation studies all six סדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה is building a puzzle. In Torah knowledge, his generation seems to have more. That should make it harder to explain why their prayers are not answered.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the משנה dealing with damages and civil law
The six orders of the משנה

phrases.english: was in Nezikin,
phrases.notes: רבה is continuing from the previous page: all the learning of רב יהודה's years was in סדר נזיקין.

phrases.english: and we learn all six orders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבה's comparison begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In breadth of Torah learning, רבה's generation surpasses רב יהודה's.

steps.title: עוקצין was very hard for רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: When רב יהודה reached difficult משניות in עוקצין, he said they felt as hard as the disputes of רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יהודה reached עוקצין, either the law of a woman pickling vegetables in a pot, or, some say, the law that olives pickled with their leaves are pure, he would say: I see the disputes of רב and שמואל here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds that even one difficult area of the משנה was very hard for רב יהודה. He gives the example of the laws about pickled food in עוקצין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רב יהודה found these laws as hard as the toughest arguments between רב and שמואל. This sharpens the contrast: in learning, the earlier generation seems weaker.

keyTerms.meaning: A tractate about stems and attached parts of produce for laws of טומאה
The difficult disputes of רב and שמואל

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין
phrases.english: And when Rav Yehuda would reach Uktzin
"a woman who pickles a vegetable in a pot,"
and some say:
"olives that were pickled with their leaves are pure,"
he would say: the disputes of Rav and Shmuel
I see here,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הֲוָה מָטֵי רַב יְהוּדָה בְּעוּקְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a concrete example of the earlier generation's limited learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even עוקצין was extremely difficult for רב יהודה.

steps.title: We know more, yet our prayers go unanswered
steps.stepSummary: רבה's generation learns עוקצין in thirteen study halls, yet רב יהודה got rain after removing one shoe, while they cry all day without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learn עוקצין in thirteen ישיבות. Yet when רב יהודה removed one shoe, rain came, and we cry out all day and no one pays attention to us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה states the puzzle clearly. His generation knows far more, yet its prayers for rain are not answered, while רב יהודה's were answered at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If Torah learning brings answered prayers, the more learned generation should succeed. The fact that it does not raises a real question: what does the earlier generation have that this one lacks?

keyTerms.meaning: Removes a shoe (a sign of fasting and distress)

phrases.english: And we learn Uktzin
in thirteen yeshivot.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ רַב יְהוּדָה, כִּי הֲוָה שָׁלֵיף חַד מְסָאנָא —
phrases.english: Whereas Rav Yehuda, when he would remove one shoe —
the rain would come,
and we cry out all day long
and there is no one who pays attention to us.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ רַב יְהוּדָה, כִּי הֲוָה שָׁלֵיף חַד מְסָאנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the learning comparison into a direct puzzle about answered prayer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that greater Torah learning should bring answered prayers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The more learned generation is ignored while the less learned one was answered immediately.

steps.title: רבה: the leaders are not at fault, the generation is unworthy
steps.stepSummary: רבה says that if anyone saw him do wrong, they should say so. The real problem is that the generation is not worthy, and the great leaders cannot fix that.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is because of deeds, if anyone saw anything wrong in me, let him say it. But what can the great ones of the generation do when their generation is not worthy?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers his own puzzle. The problem is not his personal deeds; the generation as a whole is not deserving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה rules out one explanation, his own conduct, by inviting anyone to accuse him. That leaves the other explanation: answered prayer also depends on the merit of the whole generation, not only on its leaders.

keyTerms.meaning: The great leaders of the generation

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's conclusion: even great leaders cannot bring rain when the generation itself is not worthy.

phrases.english: If it is because of deeds,
if there is anyone who saw anything — let him say so,
but what can the great ones of the generation do
when their generation is not worthy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the puzzle raised in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The difference lies in the merit of the generation, not in the leaders' deeds.

steps.title: רב יהודה sees bread being wasted and a famine follows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the story of רב יהודה's shoe. He saw two people wasting bread, concluded there was too much plenty, looked at it with anger, and a famine came.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה saw two people wasting bread. He said: Learn from this that there is plenty in the world. He set his eye on it, and there was a famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tells the background story behind the shoe and the rain that רבה mentioned. It starts with how the famine began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wasting bread showed רב יהודה that people did not value their food. His angry look was powerful enough to bring a famine, which sets up the rest of the story.

keyTerms.meaning: He set his eye (looked with anger)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יְהוּדָה חֲזָא הָנְהוּ בֵּי תְרֵי
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda saw a certain two people
who were wasting bread,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אִיכָּא שִׂבְעָא בְּעָלְמָא,
phrases.english: he said: learn from this that there is plenty in the world,
he set his eye on it — and there was a famine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה חֲזָא הָנְהוּ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story that explains רבה's reference to רב יהודה's shoe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's angry look brought a famine.

steps.title: The רבנן arrange for רב יהודה to see the market
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן asked רב יהודה's attendant, רב כהנא בריה דרב נחוניא, to lead him out by the door near the market. He did, and רב יהודה saw a crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב כהנא בריה דרב נחוניא, his attendant: You, who are often with him, should persuade him to go out by the door near the market. He persuaded him, he went out to the market, and he saw a crowd.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן want רב יהודה to see how bad the famine is. This step sets up the scene in the market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not confront רב יהודה directly. They arrange for him to see the suffering himself, hoping he will realize what has happened.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּנְיָא שַׁמָּעֵיהּ:
phrases.english: to Rav Kahana son of Rav Neḥunya, his attendant:
Master, who is often in front of him,
should persuade him to go out
by the door that is near the market.
He persuaded him, and he went out to the market,
he saw a crowd,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נְחוּנְיָא שַׁמָּעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story; the רבנן respond to the famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה is brought to the market, where he sees a crowd.

steps.title: רב יהודה asks what the crowd is
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה asks the people why they are gathered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה asks about the crowd. This question sets up the answer that will show him the famine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question lets the people's answer reveal the truth to him, just as the רבנן had planned.

phrases.english: He said to them: What is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה reacts to the crowd he saw.

steps.title: A crowd for one basket of dates shows the famine
steps.stepSummary: The people say they are standing by a basket of dates for sale. רב יהודה understands that there is a famine.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We are standing by a basket of dates that is being sold. He said: Learn from this that there is a famine in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The people answer, and רב יהודה realizes the famine is real and severe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So many people crowding around one basket of dates shows that food is very scarce. רב יהודה uses the same phrase, שמע מינה, that he used earlier. Before, it led him to conclude there was plenty; now it leads him to conclude there is famine.

phrases.english: They said to him: by a basket of dates
we are standing, which is being sold.
He said: learn from this that there is a famine in the world,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are crowding around one basket of dates, which shows there is a famine.

steps.title: One shoe removed and rain falls
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells his attendant to remove his shoes. When one shoe comes off, rain falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to his attendant: Remove my shoes. He removed one shoe, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה begins a fast for the famine by having his shoes removed. Rain falls at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the event רבה referred to in step 3. Removing even one shoe as a sign of distress was enough for Heaven to send rain.

phrases.english: He said to his attendant:
Remove my shoes for me.
He removed one shoe for him
and rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ: שְׁלוֹף לִי מְסָאנַיי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יהודה acts on his realization of the famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain fell as soon as one shoe was removed.

steps.title: אליהו stops him from removing the second shoe
steps.stepSummary: As the attendant was about to remove the second shoe, אליהו came and said in the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא that if he removed it, the world would be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came to remove the other one, אליהו came and said to him: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: If you remove the other one, I will destroy the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with אליהו stopping רב יהודה before the second shoe comes off. This shows how much weight Heaven gave to רב יהודה's distress.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the small act of removing a second shoe carried enormous power. This proves רבה's point: in רב יהודה's generation, a leader's distress was answered at once.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed be He

steps.whatToRemember: One shoe brought rain, and a second would have destroyed the world. This is the clearest proof of how quickly רב יהודה's generation was answered, compared with רבה's.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as Heaven being angry at רב יהודה. Heaven valued his distress so highly that it would not let him suffer any further.

phrases.english: When he came to remove the other one,
Elijah came and said to him:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
If you remove the other one —
I will destroy the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story begun in step 5 and illustrates רבה's point.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהודה's distress was so powerful in Heaven that one shoe brought rain and a second was not allowed.

steps.title: רב מרי sees angels turn sand into flour
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי reports that at the time of the famine and rain, he saw angels disguised as sailors fill ships with sand, and the sand became fine flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, the son of שמואל's daughter, said: I was standing on the bank of the Pappa River. I saw angels who looked like sailors. They were bringing sand and filling ships with it, and it turned into fine flour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an eyewitness report of a second miracle that happened at the same time as the famine story of רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rain from רב יהודה's shoe was one answer to the famine. רב מרי tells us that heaven also sent food right away, by turning sand into flour. This sets up his next words about whether people may buy it.

keyTerms.meaning: son of שמואל's daughter (he is known by his mother's famous father)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Shmuel's daughter, said:
I was standing
on the bank of the Pappa River.
I saw angels
who looked like sailors
who were bringing sand
and filling the ships with it,
and it became fine flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel miracle that happened during the same famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miracle of food came along with the rain: sand turned into flour.

steps.title: רב מרי tells people not to buy the miracle flour
steps.stepSummary: Everyone rushed to buy the flour, but רב מרי told them not to, since it came from a miracle. Regular wheat ships would arrive the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone came to buy it. I said to them: Do not buy from this, because it came from miracles. Tomorrow, boats of wheat will come from Parzina.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי tells the people not to use the miracle flour, and promises that normal food will come tomorrow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that one should not benefit from something made by a miracle when normal food is about to come. The miracle broke the famine, but people should still use food that comes in the ordinary way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the idea that people should avoid benefiting from miracles when they can.

phrases.english: Everyone came to buy.
I said to them:
Do not buy from this,
for it is the product of miracles.
Tomorrow will come
boats of wheat from Parzina.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב מרי's reaction to the miracle he just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not buy food made by a miracle; wait for normal food.

steps.title: רבא's fast in הגרוניא brings no rain
steps.stepSummary: רבא visits הגרוניא and decrees a fast, but no rain comes. He tells everyone to keep fasting overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא came to הגרוניא. He decreed a fast, but rain did not come. He said to them: Everyone, keep fasting through the night.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבא's fast does not work at first, so he tells the people to keep fasting through the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a fast ends at night. רבא extends it because the prayers have not been answered yet. This sets up the dream in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rava happened to come to Hagronya.
He decreed a fast,
and rain did not come.
He said to them:
Everyone, spend the night in your fast.
phrases.notes: He means: don't eat tonight; keep the fast going into the night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about prayer for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast did not work, so רבא continued it overnight.

steps.title: רבא asks if anyone had a dream
steps.stepSummary: The next morning, רבא asks whether anyone had a dream and tells them to share it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day he said to them: Is there anyone who had a dream? Let him tell it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks the people about their dreams. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא hopes a dream will show whether heaven has accepted their fast. The question opens the way for רבי אלעזר's answer.

phrases.english: The next day he said to them:
Is there anyone who saw a dream?
Let him say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the overnight fast.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether anyone received a sign in a dream.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's dream of good greetings
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר of הגרוניא reports that in his dream someone said: Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord, who does good for His people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר of הגרוניא said to them: In my dream these words were said to me: Good greetings to a good master from a good Lord, who in His goodness does good for His people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers רבא's question by sharing the message he heard in his dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The message is a greeting from 'a good Lord' (הקב"ה) to 'a good master' (רבא). It hints that heaven is ready to do good for the people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar of Hagronya said to them:
To me they recited in my dream:
Good greetings to a good master
from a good Lord,
phrases.notes: The 'good master' is רבא; the 'good Lord' is הקב"ה.

phrases.english: who from His goodness does good for His people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question about dreams.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dream message of greeting and goodness from הקב"ה.

steps.title: רבא sees a favorable time, and rain comes
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes from the dream that it is a favorable time to pray. They pray, and rain falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We can learn from this that it is a favorable time to ask for mercy. They prayed for mercy, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reads the dream as a sign, prays at the right moment, and the rain comes. This ends the הגרוניא story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fast alone did not bring rain. The dream told רבא that now was the moment heaven would accept prayer, and the prayer worked.

keyTerms.meaning: a favorable time (when prayer is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Prayer has special power at an עת רצון. רבא used the dream to recognize that moment.

phrases.english: He said: Learn from this
that it is a favorable time
(to pray for mercy).
phrases.notes: These words in round brackets are in the regular printing, but some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: They prayed for mercy, and rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עֵת רָצוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the dream.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Recognizing an עת רצון led to answered prayer and rain.

steps.title: A man dies after lashes in רבא's court
steps.stepSummary: A man received lashes in רבא's court for relations with a non-Jewish woman, and he died. King שבור heard and wanted to punish רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man was sentenced to lashes in רבא's court because he had relations with a non-Jewish woman. רבא gave him lashes, and he died. The matter was heard in the house of King שבור, and he wanted to punish רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבא is in danger from the Persian king because a man died from lashes in his court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king sees this as a death sentence carried out without his permission. This sets up the danger that the queen mother will try to prevent.

phrases.english: A certain man
who was sentenced to lashes
in Rava's court
because he had relations with a gentile woman.
Rava flogged him, and he died.
The matter was heard in the house of King Shapur;
he wanted to punish Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאִיחַיַּיב נְגָדָא בְּבֵי דִינָא דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story that will also involve prayer for rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא is in danger from the king.

steps.title: The king's mother warns him about the Jews
steps.stepSummary: איפרא הורמיז, the king's mother, tells him not to fight with the Jews, because their God gives them whatever they ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: איפרא הורמיז, the mother of King שבור, said to her son: Don't get into any dispute with the Jews, because whatever they ask from their Master, He gives them.
steps.whatsHappening: The queen mother tries to protect רבא by warning her son that the Jews' prayers are answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her argument is that harming the Jews is dangerous, since God listens to them. This claim leads to the king's questions in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: איפרא הורמיז, mother of King שבור

phrases.english: Ifra Hormiz said to him,
the mother of King Shapur, to her son:
Do not have any dispute
with the Jews,
for whatever they ask from their Master
He gives them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ אִיפְרָא הוֹרְמִיז אִימֵּיהּ דְּשַׁבּוּר מַלְכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the king's plan to punish רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Jews' requests are answered by God, so do not harm them.

steps.title: The king asks for an example
steps.stepSummary: שבור asks his mother what she means by this.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The king asks his mother for an example of God giving the Jews what they ask. This sets up her answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He wants evidence before he accepts her claim.

phrases.english: He said to her:
What is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions his mother's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: An example of the Jews' prayers being answered.

steps.title: They pray and rain comes
steps.stepSummary: The mother answers that when the Jews pray for mercy, rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They pray for mercy, and rain comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The queen mother gives her example: the Jews pray for rain and get it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the story to the topic of the whole section, rain in answer to prayer.

phrases.english: They pray for mercy,
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips 'she said'; this is the mother answering.

phrases.english: and rain comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the king's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their prayers for rain are answered.

steps.title: The king says rain in the rainy season proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: שבור argues that rain in its season is no proof. A real test would be for them to pray in the summer month of תמוז and have rain come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: That happens because it is the rainy season. Rather, let them pray for mercy now, in the season of תמוז, and let rain come.
steps.whatsHappening: The king challenges his mother's proof and proposes a harder test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain that falls in the rainy season could be nature, not an answer to prayer. Rain in תמוז, the dry summer, would be a clear sign that God answers the Jews.

phrases.english: He said to her:
That is because it is the time for rain.
Rather, let them pray for mercy now,
in the season of Tammuz,
and let rain come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the mother's proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that rain after prayer proves God answers the Jews.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain in the rainy season can be explained by nature, so a real test would need rain out of season.

steps.title: רבא prays for summer rain, and none comes
steps.stepSummary: איפרא הורמיז asks רבא to pray with focus for rain. He prays, but no rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: She sent a message to רבא: Focus your mind and pray for mercy that rain should come. He prayed for mercy, and rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The queen mother asks רבא to take the king's test. At first his prayer fails, which sets up what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on this prayer: רבא's safety and the honor of the Jews. No rain comes at first, which sets up רבא's second prayer in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: The story is not over here. Do not think the test failed for good, because the גמרא continues the story right after this.

phrases.english: She sent a message to Rava:
Focus your mind
and pray for mercy that rain should come.
He prayed for mercy, and rain did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the test the king proposed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's first prayer for summer rain is not answered.

steps.title: רבא prays again and heavy rain falls
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a פסוק saying our fathers told us of God's wonders but we never saw them ourselves. Rain falls so hard that the gutters of מחוזא overflow into the דיגלת river.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before God: Master of the Universe! 'O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers told us of the work You did in their days, in days of old,' but we have not seen it with our own eyes! Rain came until the gutters of מחוזא poured into the דיגלת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's first prayer did not work, so he prays again, this time quoting a פסוק from תהלים. Now a huge rain comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's argument is that the miracles we only hear about from earlier generations should also be seen in our days. The rain answers שבור's challenge from Step 21: rain in תמוז, outside its season. The size of the rain, filling the gutters into the river, shows clearly that this was a real answer to prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the Universe, a way of speaking directly to God
the work You did, meaning God's miracles
the city of מחוזא, where רבא lived

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
phrases.notes: The 'he' is רבא, who has just prayed once with no rain.

phrases.english: "O God, we have heard with our ears,
our fathers have told us
of the work You did in their days, in days of old,"
but we have not seen it with our own eyes!
Rain came
until the gutters of Mechoza poured out into the Tigris.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after the failed first prayer, רבא prays again and succeeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's second prayer brings heavy rain in תמוז, meeting שבור's test.

steps.title: רבא's father warns him in a dream
steps.stepSummary: רבא's late father appears to him in a dream, says he has troubled Heaven too much, and tells him to change where he sleeps. The next day רבא finds his old bed slashed with knives.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father came and appeared to him in a dream and said to him: Is there anyone who troubles Heaven this much? He said to him: Change your place. He changed his place, and the next day he found his bed slashed with knives.
steps.whatsHappening: The story has a dangerous ending: רבא is warned in a dream that pushing Heaven so hard for rain was risky. He moves his bed and is saved from an attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's words show that bringing rain out of its season was seen as asking too much of Heaven. The slashed bed shows that there really was danger, and the warning saved רבא's life.

keyTerms.meaning: who troubles, who puts a burden on

steps.whatToRemember: רבא succeeded in bringing rain in תמוז, but his father warned him that he had pushed Heaven too far, and he was saved only by moving his bed.

phrases.english: His father came and appeared to him in his dream
and said to him: Is there anyone who troubles
Heaven this much?
He said to him: Change your place.
He changed his place,
and the next day he found his bed slashed with knives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the רבא story by showing the danger of his bold prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forcing rain out of its season was seen as troubling Heaven too much and put רבא in danger.

steps.title: רב פפא's fast fails to bring rain
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא declares a fast, but no rain comes. Feeling weak, he eats a bowl of porridge and prays, and still no rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא decreed a fast, but rain did not come. He felt weak, swallowed a bowl of porridge, and prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about praying for rain. This step sets up the problem: רב פפא's fast and prayer are not working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two details are added: the fast did not help, and רב פפא ate during the fast because he felt weak. That second detail sets up what happens next, when someone mocks him for it.

keyTerms.meaning: his heart became weak, he felt faint

phrases.english: Rav Pappa decreed a fast
but rain did not come.
He felt weak, so he swallowed a bowl of porridge
and prayed for mercy, but rain did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about prayer for rain, after the רבא story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא's fast and prayer did not bring rain.

steps.title: רב פפא is embarrassed and the rain comes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר אושפזתי mocks רב פפא, saying another bowl of porridge would bring rain. רב פפא is embarrassed and upset, and then the rain comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר אושפזתי said to him: If the Master swallows another bowl of porridge, rain will come. He was embarrassed and upset, and rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone teases רב פפא for eating during the fast. His embarrassment and hurt feelings are what finally bring the rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fasting alone did not work, but רב פפא's broken, humbled feeling did. The story shows that a humble, hurt heart can bring an answer when regular prayer did not.

keyTerms.meaning: his mind became weak, he felt upset and low
Master, a respectful way to say 'you'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אוּשְׁפַּזְתִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Ushpazti said to him:
If the Master swallows another bowl
of porridge, rain will come.
He was embarrassed and grew upset, and rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר אוּשְׁפַּזְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רב פפא story: the mockery leads to his humbling, which brings the rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא's embarrassment and broken heart brought the rain that his fast had not.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן דוסא stops and starts the rain
steps.stepSummary: While traveling, רבי חנינא בן דוסא complains that the whole world is comfortable but he is suffering in the rain, and it stops. At home he says the world is suffering while he is comfortable, and the rain returns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was traveling on the road when rain came. He said before God: Master of the Universe, the whole world is comfortable and חנינא is suffering! The rain stopped. When he reached his home, he said: Master of the Universe, the whole world is suffering and חנינא is comfortable? The rain came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another rain story, showing how strong רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayers were. With just a few words he could make rain stop and start again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The world needed the rain, but it bothered רבי חנינא while he traveled, so he asked for it to stop just for him. Once he was home, he asked for it to come back for everyone. The story sets up רב יוסף's comment in the next step about how powerful his prayers were.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא, אֲתָא מִיטְרָא.
phrases.english: was traveling on the road, and rain came.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
the entire world is comfortable,
but Chanina is suffering! The rain stopped.
When he arrived at his home,
he said before Him: Master of the Universe,
the entire world is suffering
and Chanina is comfortable? The rain came.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate story about prayer and rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's short prayers could stop and restart the rain.

steps.title: רב יוסף compares the כהן גדול's prayer to רבי חנינא בן דוסא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the prayer of the כהן גדול was no match for רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer. He brings a משנה that the כהן גדול said a short prayer in the outer chamber.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What use is the prayer of the כהן גדול against רבי חנינא בן דוסא? As we learned in a משנה: He would pray a short prayer in the outer chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף reacts to the story by saying that even the כהן גדול's prayer could not beat רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer. This sets up the next questions about what the כהן גדול actually prayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make his point, רב יוסף points to a משנה about the short prayer the כהן גדול said on יום כיפור. We still do not know what that prayer said, so the גמרא will ask that next.

keyTerms.meaning: what use is it, what does it accomplish
as we learned in a משנה
the outer chamber of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not putting down the כהן גדול. He is praising רבי חנינא בן דוסא by saying his prayer was even stronger.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי אַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What effect does
the prayer of the High Priest have
against Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa?
As we learned: He would pray a short prayer
in the outer chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי אַהְנְיָא לֵיהּ צְלוֹתָא דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the רבי חנינא בן דוסא story by comparing it to the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול's prayer could not overpower the prayer of רבי חנינא בן דוסא.

steps.title: What did the כהן גדול pray?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words of the כהן גדול's short prayer were.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would he pray?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: what did the כהן גדול say in that short prayer? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said that he prayed a short prayer, not what it said. To understand רב יוסף's comparison, we need to know the words.

phrases.english: What would he pray?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the content of the prayer mentioned in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact words of the כהן גדול's short prayer.

steps.title: The כהן גדול prayed for a rainy and hot year
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר אדא and רבא בר אדא, in the name of רב יהודה, say the prayer was: May it be Your will that this year be rainy and hot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר אדא and רבא בר אדא both said in the name of רב יהודה: May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that this year be rainy and hot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving the words of the כהן גדול's prayer. He asked for a year that is rainy and hot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer brings in two new parts: rain, which fits the topic, and heat, which seems strange. That strange part leads straight to the next question.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִין בַּר אַדָּא וְרָבָא בַּר אַדָּא
phrases.english: Ravin bar Adda and Rava bar Adda
who both say in the name of Rav Yehuda:
May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that this year shall be rainy and hot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִין בַּר אַדָּא וְרָבָא בַּר אַדָּא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the כהן גדול prayed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He prayed that the year be rainy and hot.

steps.title: Why would heat be a good thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the prayer: is heat a good thing? On the contrary, it is bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is heat a good thing? On the contrary, it is a bad thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that the כהן גדול would ask for a hot year. It challenges this part of the prayer, and the next step answers by rewording it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking for rain makes sense, but heat usually harms crops and people. So it seems odd that a holy prayer on יום כיפור would ask for heat, and the גמרא will need to explain it.

phrases.english: Is heat a good thing?
On the contrary, it is a bad thing!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחוּנָה מְעַלַּיְיתָא הִיא? אַדְּרַבָּה, גְּרִיעוּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'hot' in the prayer just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word שחונה (hot) in the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heat is normally harmful, so it makes no sense to pray for it.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: if the year is hot, let it be rainy and moist
steps.stepSummary: Because heat alone is bad, the גמרא rewords the prayer: if the year is going to be hot, may it also be rainy and full of dew.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the prayer was: If the year is hot, let it be rainy and moist with dew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own challenge from the last step by fixing the words of the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 asked how the כהן גדול could pray for heat, since heat hurts crops. The answer is that he did not ask for heat. He said that if the year is already going to be hot, it should also have rain and dew so the crops are not harmed.

phrases.english: Rather: if it is hot,
phrases.notes: He is not asking for heat. He means: if the year turns out hot anyway.

phrases.english: let it be rainy and moist with dew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31 by rewording the prayer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prayer asked outright for a hot year, which seems harmful.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prayer only asked that a hot year also be rainy and moist, so the crops stay safe.

steps.title: The prayer asks that travelers' prayers not be accepted
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול also prayed that the prayers of travelers should not come before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let the prayer of travelers not come before You.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the כהן גדול's prayer with a line about travelers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Travelers would pray for the rain to stop so they would not get wet, but the world needs rain. This line explains רב יוסף's point in step 28. The כהן גדול asked that travelers not be listened to, yet when רבי חנינא בן דוסא traveled and prayed, the rain stopped anyway (step 27).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key to the whole section. It shows how רבי חנינא's prayer was stronger than the כהן גדול's.

phrases.english: And let not enter before You
the prayer of travelers.
phrases.notes: Think back to step 27: רבי חנינא was a traveler, and his prayer for the rain to stop worked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַל יִכָּנֵס לְפָנֶיךָ תְּפִילַּת עוֹבְרֵי דְּרָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same prayer begun in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול asked that travelers' prayers against rain not be accepted. This explains why רבי חנינא's accepted prayer outweighed his.

steps.title: רב אחא adds the closing lines of the prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא, in the name of רב יהודה, finishes the prayer: may rule stay with the house of יהודה, and may Israel not need to depend on each other or on another nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא concluded the prayer in the name of רב יהודה: May ruling power not leave the house of יהודה, and may Your nation Israel not need to be supported by one another, nor by another nation.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds the ending of the כהן גדול's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds two more requests: that leadership stay with the Jewish people, and that the people have enough of their own so no one needs handouts from others. It completes the prayer and does not change the earlier parts.

keyTerms.meaning: To be supported, to earn a living

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול's prayer covered good weather, ignoring travelers' requests against rain, Jewish leadership, and that Israel not depend on handouts.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, concludes
in the name of Rav Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: לָא יִעְדֵּי עָבֵיד שׁוּלְטָן מִדְּבֵית יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: May the one who wields rule not depart from the house of Judah,
and may Your nation Israel not be
in need of being supported by one another,
nor by another nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְסַיֵּים מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final lines to the prayer quoted in steps 30-33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prayer ended with requests for Jewish rule and for Israel to be self-supporting.

steps.title: The world is fed in רבי חנינא's merit, yet he lives on carobs
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: every day a בת קול says the whole world is fed because of רבי חנינא, while he himself gets by on a קב of carobs from one Friday to the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Every single day a בת קול goes out and says: The whole world is fed because of My son חנינא, and My son חנינא is satisfied with a קב of carobs from one ערב שבת to the next.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new statement praising רבי חנינא בן דוסא's greatness and simple life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a sharp contrast here. Because of his merit, food comes down to the whole world, but he himself has almost nothing, only a small measure of cheap carobs for a whole week.

keyTerms.meaning: A small measure of carobs, a cheap food

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת וְאוֹמֶרֶת:
phrases.english: Each and every day a heavenly voice goes out and says:
The entire world is fed
for the sake of My son Ḥanina,
and for My son Ḥanina a kav of carobs is enough
from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּכׇל יוֹם וְיוֹם בַּת קוֹל יוֹצֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the prayer to a new teaching about רבי חנינא בן דוסא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא's merit feeds the whole world while he lives in extreme poverty.

steps.title: Story begins: רבי חנינא's wife heats the oven every Friday
steps.stepSummary: The story starts: every Friday, רבי חנינא's wife would heat the oven and throw in something to make smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife would regularly heat the oven every ערב שבת and throw in something that makes smoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about רבי חנינא's poor household. This line sets the scene, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They had no food to bake, so why heat the oven and make smoke? The story does not explain yet. This is only the setup, and the reason comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: His wife was accustomed
to heat the oven every Shabbat eve
and throw in something to make smoke

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a story showing the poverty described in step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup of a story: the wife heated an empty oven every Friday and made smoke.
